author: Alex Michaelides
review: A gripping psychological thriller about a woman who stops speaking after allegedly murdering her husband. The twist ending recontextualizes everything you've read and will keep you thinking long after the last page.

author: James Clear
review: A practical, well-structured guide to building good habits and breaking bad ones through tiny daily improvements. The real-life examples make the ideas easy to apply immediately.

author: Frank Herbert
review: An epic science fiction masterpiece blending politics, religion, and ecology on the desert planet Arrakis. Dense and demanding at times, but the world-building is unmatched.

bookName: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
review: A thought-provoking journey through human history, from the Stone Age to the modern era. Harari challenges common assumptions about money, religion, and progress in an engaging way.

author: Paulo Coelho
review: A simple yet inspiring fable about a shepherd boy chasing his dream across the desert. Its gentle wisdom about destiny and listening to your heart makes it a comforting, quick read.

author: Jane Austen
review: A witty and timeless romance following Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy as pride and first impressions stand in the way of love. Austen's sharp social commentary still feels fresh today.

author: Gillian Flynn
review: A dark, twisty thriller told from alternating perspectives after a wife disappears on her fifth anniversary. Sharp, unsettling, and impossible to put down once the secrets begin to unravel.
